messages:
rachel: Hi all  day 1! I grabbed the kubeconfig from the onboarding portal and followed the quickstart but `kubectl get pods -n platform-tools` times out:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n platform-tools
Unable to connect to the server: dial tcp 10.12.34.78:6443: i/o timeout
```
Is there a specific VPN or proxy I need to use to reach the cluster? Also who do I ping for namespace access?

omar: welcome @rachel! usually timeout means either you're on corp network that rewrites TLS, or you need to route via our bastion. Quick triage: can you `curl -v https://10.12.34.78:6443` and paste the TLS subject? If you see a proxy banner that's the issue. For access requests use https://redwood.internal/access-requests and request `platform-tools` with role `k8s:developer`. Approver will be your manager by default.

rachel: curl shows a corp-proxy banner. I think our laptop is on the internal network.

infra-bot: Access request #AK-15001 created for user rachel. Approver: @ben. Status: pending. Link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/AK-15001

ben: hi @rachel, I can fast-track once you DM me your GitHub handle. Also for TLS/proxy we prefer using the SSH SOCKS bastion so you don't need to change OS trust stores. Steps: 
1) ssh -D 1080 bastion@jump.redwood.local -N
2) export ALL_PROXY=socks5://localhost:1080
3) KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config kubectl get pods -n platform-tools
If you want, I can add a comment to your ticket to allow bastion route for 7 days.

rachel: sent you a DM with my GitHub handle (rach-dev). Tried the bastion steps and `kubectl get pods` now returns `Forbidden` with `system:anonymous`.

omar: anonymous means the kubeconfig doesn't include the OIDC exec plugin/token. Run `kubectl config view --raw` and check the user block for `exec` or `token`. If it's missing, re-download the kubeconfig from the portal choosing the OIDC option, or we can patch it.

ben: approved AK-15001 (temp bind for 72h). @oncall-bot please create a temporary binding `onboard-rachel`->`platform-tools` with `edit` for 72h.

oncall-bot: Temporary RBAC binding onboard-rachel -> namespace platform-tools created. Expires in 259200 seconds. Ticket: AK-15001

rachel: after bind I re-downloaded the kubeconfig OIDC option and now `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n platform-tools` returns `yes`. Thanks for the fast help! One quick Q: how do I create a context that always uses the namespace so I don't have to pass `-n`?

omar: run `kubectl config set-context rachel-platform --namespace=platform-tools --cluster=redwood-dev@redwood-cluster --user=rach-dev` and then `kubectl config use-context rachel-platform`. Also avoid running destructive commands without a review in that namespace. If you need to port-forward: `kubectl -n platform-tools port-forward svc/dev-dashboard 8080:80` and use the bastion SOCKS while developing.

ben: Glad that's resolved. @rachel welcome to Redwood Inference! If you hit anything else, drop it here or ping infra oncall.

rachel: thanks everyone :wave: feeling set up now :)
